materials.title_en: Don't Throw It Away — Fix It
materials.summary_zh: 一篇社区报道：小区里的“修理咖啡馆”每月开一次，志愿者免费帮居民修东西。（虚构报道）

segments.en: On the first Saturday of every month, the community centre on Elm Road turns into a repair café.
segments.zh: 每个月的第一个周六，榆树路的社区中心都会变成一家“修理咖啡馆”。

segments.en: Local people bring broken things, such as lamps, toasters, bikes and torn jackets.
segments.zh: 附近的居民把坏了的东西带来，比如台灯、烤面包机、自行车和破了的夹克。

segments.en: Volunteers with useful skills try to fix them for free, while visitors drink tea and wait.
segments.zh: 有一技之长的志愿者免费帮忙修理，来访的人一边喝茶一边等。

segments.en: The café started two years ago, when a retired engineer called Peter Hall noticed how much his neighbours threw away.
segments.zh: 这家咖啡馆两年前开办。当时，一位名叫 Peter Hall 的退休工程师注意到邻居们扔掉的东西实在太多了。

segments.en: "Most things only need a small repair," he says. "However, people think it's easier to buy something new."
segments.zh: “大多数东西只需要小修一下，”他说，“可是人们觉得买个新的更省事。”

segments.en: Last year the volunteers repaired more than six hundred items, and about seventy percent of them worked again.
segments.zh: 去年，志愿者修了六百多件东西，其中大约七成修好后又能用了。

segments.en: Visitors are also encouraged to watch and learn, so next time they can do the repair themselves.
segments.zh: 来访的人也被鼓励在旁边看、跟着学，这样下次就能自己修了。

segments.en: Although the repairs are free, many people leave a small donation to pay for tools and spare parts.
segments.zh: 虽然修理是免费的，很多人还是会留下一点捐款，用来买工具和零件。

segments.en: Not everything can be saved, of course, and some modern devices are almost impossible to open.
segments.zh: 当然，并不是所有东西都能修好，有些新式电子设备几乎打不开。

segments.en: Still, Peter believes the café does more than fix objects: "People talk, share skills and make friends here."
segments.zh: 不过，Peter 认为咖啡馆的意义不止是修东西：“人们在这里聊天、分享手艺、交朋友。”

glossary.zh: 撕破的（tear 的过去分词）

glossary.note_zh: threw 是 throw 的过去式。

glossary.zh: 被鼓励（encourage 的过去分词）
glossary.note_zh: be encouraged to do = 被鼓励做某事

questions.explanation_zh: 原文：about seventy percent of them worked again.

questions.explanation_zh: 原文：to pay for tools and spare parts.

options: 让人们交流、分享手艺、交朋友

materials.summary_zh: 一篇个人博客：作者四十岁开始学西班牙语，讲她遇到的困难、找到的办法，以及她对“年纪大了学不好”的看法。（虚构博客）

segments.en: When I turned forty, I decided to learn Spanish, and many friends told me it was too late.
segments.zh: 四十岁那年，我决定学西班牙语，很多朋友都说我太晚了。

segments.en: In my opinion, they were wrong, although the first months were harder than I expected.
segments.zh: 在我看来他们错了，尽管头几个月比我想象的难。

segments.en: My memory isn't as quick as it was at school, so new words disappeared from my head overnight.
segments.zh: 我的记性没有上学时那么好，新单词过一夜就忘了。

segments.en: However, I soon found that adults have some advantages too.
segments.zh: 不过，我很快发现成年人也有一些优势。

segments.en: For example, I know exactly why I'm learning, and I can plan my time much better than a teenager.
segments.zh: 比如，我很清楚自己为什么学，安排时间的能力也比青少年强得多。

segments.en: I also stopped trying to learn everything at once.
segments.zh: 我也不再试图一下子什么都学。

segments.en: Instead, I study for twenty minutes every morning and review old words before I learn new ones.
segments.zh: 相反，我每天早上学二十分钟，学新单词之前先复习旧的。

segments.en: The biggest change came when I started speaking, even though I made lots of mistakes.
segments.zh: 最大的变化发生在我开始开口说的时候，尽管我犯了很多错。

segments.en: A teacher told me that if I waited until I was perfect, I would never speak at all.
segments.zh: 一位老师对我说，要是等到完美再开口，我就永远不会开口了。

segments.en: Two years later, I can chat with my neighbours in Valencia and follow most of the news.
segments.zh: 两年后，我能和瓦伦西亚的邻居聊天，也能听懂大部分新闻了。

segments.en: So, is it too late at forty? I don't think so, but you need patience and a plan.
segments.zh: 那么，四十岁学太晚吗？我不这么认为，不过你需要耐心和计划。

glossary.zh: 预料；预想（expect 的过去式）

questions.explanation_zh: 原文：many friends told me it was too late.

options: 不晚，但需要耐心和计划
只有住在国外才能学好

materials.title_en: Your First Week at a New Job
materials.summary_zh: 一档职场播客：主持人请一位人事经理谈谈入职第一周该注意什么。（虚构节目）

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Welcome back to Work Talk. Today Grace, an HR manager, is here with advice for your first week in a new job.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到《职场谈》。今天人事经理 Grace 来给大家讲讲新工作第一周的建议。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: Thanks for having me. My first tip is simple: arrive a little early, especially on the first day.
segments.zh: 谢谢邀请。我的第一条建议很简单：早点到，尤其是第一天。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Why does that matter so much?
segments.zh: 这为什么那么重要？

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: If you arrive early, you'll have time to find the right office and calm down before you meet everyone.
segments.zh: 早点到的话，你有时间找到办公室，见大家之前也能平静下来。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: What about all the new names? I always forget them.
segments.zh: 那么多新名字怎么办？我总是记不住。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: Most people do. Write them down with a short note, for example 'Tom, design, loves cycling'.
segments.zh: 大多数人都记不住。把名字写下来，加一句简短的备注，比如“Tom，设计部，喜欢骑车”。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: And don't be afraid to ask questions. Nobody expects you to know everything in week one.
segments.zh: 还有，别怕提问。没人指望你第一周就什么都懂。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: But some people worry that questions make them look weak.
segments.zh: 可有些人担心提问会显得自己能力不够。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: Actually, it's the opposite. Unless you ask, your manager won't know where you need help.
segments.zh: 其实恰恰相反。你不问，经理就不知道你哪里需要帮助。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Any advice about lunch? That can feel awkward.
segments.zh: 午饭方面有什么建议吗？那有时挺尴尬的。

segments.speaker: Grace
segments.en: If someone invites you, say yes, even if you're busy. Lunch is where you really get to know the team.
segments.zh: 要是有人邀请你，即使忙也答应。午饭才是真正了解团队的时候。

segments.speaker: Host
segments.en: Great tips. Thanks, Grace.
segments.zh: 很棒的建议。谢谢你，Grace。

glossary.zh: 人力资源经理；人事经理

glossary.note_zh: write something down = 写下来、记下来
be afraid to do = 不敢做

materials.summary_zh: 两位邻居讨论小区门口要修的自行车道：一个支持，一个担心停车问题，最后找到了共同点。（虚构对话）

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: Did you read the letter from the council? They want to build a bike lane on our street.
segments.zh: 你看到市政府的信了吗？他们想在我们这条街上修自行车道。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Yes, and I think it's a great idea. I cycle to work, and the traffic here is really dangerous.
segments.zh: 看到了，我觉得这主意很好。我骑车上班，这里的交通真的很危险。

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: I see your point. But they're going to remove twenty parking spaces.
segments.zh: 我明白你的意思。可他们要拆掉二十个停车位。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: That's true. Where will people park, then?
segments.zh: 这倒是。那大家停在哪儿呢？

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: Exactly. My mum visits every weekend, and she can't walk far.
segments.zh: 就是啊。我妈每个周末都来，她走不了远路。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Although parking will be harder, I think fewer people will need cars if cycling feels safe.
segments.zh: 虽然停车会更难，但我觉得如果骑车让人觉得安全，需要开车的人就会变少。

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: Maybe in the long term. However, that won't help my mum next month.
segments.zh: 长远来看也许吧。不过这对我妈下个月来没什么帮助。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Fair point. What if we asked the council for a few spaces for older and disabled drivers?
segments.zh: 有道理。要是我们请市政府留几个给老年人和残障司机的车位呢？

segments.speaker: Ben
segments.en: That would solve my main problem. I'd support the lane if they did that.
segments.zh: 那就解决了我最大的问题。要是他们这么做，我就支持修车道。

segments.speaker: Rosa
segments.en: Great. Let's write to them together this week.
segments.zh: 太好了。我们这周一起给他们写信吧。

materials.title_en: The City That Fell in Love with Bikes
materials.summary_zh: 一篇城市报道：里弗顿推出共享单车三年后的变化，以及仍然存在的不满。（虚构报道）

segments.en: Three years ago, the city of Riverton introduced a bike-sharing scheme with 500 bikes and 40 stations.
segments.zh: 三年前，里弗顿市推出了共享单车计划，有 500 辆车和 40 个站点。

segments.en: Many people expected it to fail, because the city is hilly and it rains a lot.
segments.zh: 很多人预计它会失败，因为这座城市坡多，而且经常下雨。

segments.en: However, the scheme has been far more popular than anyone imagined.
segments.zh: 然而，这个计划比任何人想象的都受欢迎得多。

segments.en: Today there are 2,000 bikes, and about half of them are electric, which makes the hills much easier.
segments.zh: 如今有 2000 辆车，大约一半是电动的，上坡轻松多了。

segments.en: Users pay a small monthly fee and can take a bike from any station for up to 45 minutes.
segments.zh: 用户每月付一小笔费用，就可以从任何站点借车，每次最长 45 分钟。

segments.en: According to the council, car traffic in the city centre has fallen by twelve percent.
segments.zh: 据市政府说，市中心的汽车流量下降了 12%。

segments.en: Shop owners were worried at first, but most now say that cyclists stop and spend money more often than drivers.
segments.zh: 店主们起初很担心，但大多数人现在说，骑车的人比开车的人更常停下来消费。

segments.en: Not everyone is happy, though.
segments.zh: 不过，并不是每个人都满意。

segments.en: Some residents complain that bikes are left on pavements, and others say the scheme should reach the suburbs too.
segments.zh: 一些居民抱怨自行车被乱停在人行道上，还有人说这个计划也应该扩展到郊区。

segments.en: The council plans to add 30 new stations next year, mostly outside the centre.
segments.zh: 市政府计划明年新增 30 个站点，大多在市中心以外。

segments.en: For now, the bikes seem to be here to stay.
segments.zh: 就目前来看，这些自行车似乎会一直留下来。

materials.summary_zh: 一篇博客：作者在希腊做保护海龟的志愿者，讲工作内容、辛苦之处和难忘的一刻。

segments.en: Last summer, instead of lying on a beach, I spent two weeks protecting one.
segments.zh: 去年夏天，我没有躺在海滩上度假，而是花了两周去保护一片海滩。

segments.en: I joined a volunteer project in Greece that looks after sea turtles and their nests.
segments.zh: 我参加了希腊的一个志愿项目，照顾海龟和它们的巢。

segments.en: Our day started at six in the morning, before the sand got too hot.
segments.zh: 我们每天早上六点开始工作，趁沙子还不太烫。

segments.en: We walked along the beach looking for new turtle tracks, then marked and protected any nests we found.
segments.zh: 我们沿着海滩寻找新的海龟爬痕，然后标记并保护找到的巢。

segments.en: In the afternoons, we talked to tourists and explained why they shouldn't leave umbrellas or rubbish on the sand.
segments.zh: 下午我们和游客交流，解释为什么不应该把遮阳伞或垃圾留在沙滩上。

segments.en: Most people were interested, and some even came back the next day to help.
segments.zh: 大多数人很感兴趣，有些人第二天甚至回来帮忙。

segments.en: The work was harder than I expected, and the accommodation was very basic: a tent and a cold shower.
segments.zh: 工作比我预想的辛苦，住宿也很简陋：一顶帐篷加冷水淋浴。

segments.en: But on my last night, I watched about fifty baby turtles come out of a nest and run towards the sea.
segments.zh: 但在最后一晚，我看着大约五十只小海龟从巢里爬出来，奔向大海。

segments.en: It was one of the best moments of my life.
segments.zh: 那是我人生中最美好的时刻之一。

segments.en: If you are thinking about volunteering, choose a project that is honest about the work and the conditions.
segments.zh: 如果你在考虑做志愿者，选一个对工作内容和条件说实话的项目。

glossary.note_zh: 形容住宿时指条件简单

materials.summary_zh: 一篇杂志文章：睡前看屏幕为什么影响睡眠，以及几个简单的改善办法。

segments.en: Do you check your phone in bed? If so, you are not alone.
segments.zh: 你在床上看手机吗？如果是，你并不孤单。

segments.en: In a recent survey, seven out of ten young adults said they use a screen during the last hour before sleep.
segments.zh: 在最近一项调查中，十个年轻人里有七个说他们在睡前最后一小时会用屏幕。

segments.en: Doctors say this habit can make it harder to fall asleep, for two main reasons.
segments.zh: 医生说，这个习惯会让人更难入睡，主要有两个原因。

segments.en: First, the light from screens tells the brain that it is still daytime.
segments.zh: 第一，屏幕的光会告诉大脑现在还是白天。

segments.en: Second, and probably more important, what we read or watch keeps our minds busy.
segments.zh: 第二，可能也更重要的是，我们读的、看的内容让大脑一直处于忙碌状态。

segments.en: A worrying email or an exciting video is not the best way to relax.
segments.zh: 一封让人担心的邮件或一个刺激的视频，可不是放松的好办法。

segments.en: So what can you do?
segments.zh: 那该怎么办呢？

segments.en: Experts suggest putting your phone in another room, or at least out of reach, about an hour before bed.
segments.zh: 专家建议睡前大约一小时把手机放到另一个房间，或者至少放到够不着的地方。

segments.en: If you use your phone as an alarm, buy a cheap alarm clock instead.
segments.zh: 如果你用手机当闹钟，那就买个便宜的闹钟代替。

segments.en: Reading a paper book or listening to quiet music can help your body prepare for sleep.
segments.zh: 读纸质书或听轻音乐，能帮助身体为睡眠做准备。

segments.en: It may feel strange for a few nights, but most people say they sleep better within a week.
segments.zh: 头几个晚上可能会不习惯，但大多数人说一周之内就睡得更好了。

questions.explanation_zh: 原文：seven out of ten young adults said they use a screen during the last hour before sleep.

questions.prompt_zh: 屏幕影响睡眠的第一个原因是什么？
options: 屏幕的光让大脑以为还是白天
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：the light from screens tells the brain that it is still daytime.

questions.prompt_zh: 作者认为可能更重要的原因是什么？
options: 读的看的内容让大脑一直很忙
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：Second, and probably more important, what we read or watch keeps our minds busy.

questions.prompt_zh: 用手机当闹钟的人应该怎么做？
options: 买一个便宜的闹钟代替
questions.explanation_zh: 原文：buy a cheap alarm clock instead.

materials.summary_zh: 办公室经理发给全体员工的邮件：搬迁的时间、员工要做的准备和新办公室的情况。

segments.en: Subject: Office move – what you need to know
segments.zh: 主题：办公室搬迁——你需要知道的事

segments.en: Hi everyone,
segments.zh: 大家好：

segments.en: As you know, we are moving to our new office on Bridge Street at the end of this month.
segments.zh: 大家都知道，我们这个月底要搬到桥街的新办公室。

segments.en: The move will take place over the weekend of the 28th, so the office will be closed on Friday the 27th.
segments.zh: 搬迁将在 28 号那个周末进行，所以 27 号周五办公室关闭。

segments.en: Please work from home that day.
segments.zh: 那天请在家办公。

segments.en: Before you leave on Thursday, pack your personal things into the boxes that will be delivered on Monday.
segments.zh: 周四下班前，请把个人物品装进周一会送来的箱子里。

segments.en: Write your name and desk number clearly on each box.
segments.zh: 在每个箱子上清楚地写上你的名字和工位号。

segments.en: IT will move all computers, so you don't need to unplug anything yourself.
segments.zh: IT 部门会搬所有电脑，所以你不需要自己拔任何插头。

segments.en: The new office has more meeting rooms, a bigger kitchen and showers for people who cycle to work.
segments.zh: 新办公室有更多会议室、更大的厨房，还有供骑车上班的人用的淋浴间。

segments.en: It is also only five minutes' walk from the station.
segments.zh: 它离车站也只有五分钟步行路程。

segments.en: Parking spaces will be limited, so please use public transport if you can.
segments.zh: 停车位会很有限，所以请尽量乘坐公共交通。

segments.en: If you have any questions, please contact me before Wednesday.
segments.zh: 如有任何问题，请在周三之前联系我。

segments.en: Thanks for your help, Karen (Office Manager)
segments.zh: 谢谢大家的配合，凯伦（办公室经理）
